text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Four youths with the opposition National Development Party led by Raila Odinga are arrested in connection with the killing of a policeman in Nairobi last Friday.
- Armed gangsters wearing police uniforms raid a Nairobi petrol station and escape with more than 650,000 Kenyan shillings.
- The opposition-backed National Convention Executive Council lobby group suspends mass action to give religious leaders time to arrange talks with the ruling party.
- President Daniel arap Moi says the government will step up its efforts to track down those involved in mayhem that led to the killing of two police officers and a civilian on Friday.
- Seventy-two houses are burned and 20 people seriously injured in four days of violence in a Nairobi slum.
- Shops in Nairobi are temporarily closed in panic when more than 250 hawkers demonstrate, complaining of harassment by city authorities.
- The government-appointed Standing Committee on Human Rights expresses deep concern over the breakdown of law and order during a drive for constitutional reforms.
- The minister of foreign affairs dismisses the possibility of the appointment of a coalition government in Kenya.
- Nairobi's police boss orders an investigation into allegations that suspected thieves from slums are being protected by some police officers. ($1=70.48 Kenyan shillings)
